'''Ofer Lahav''' ({{langx|he|עופר להב}}) {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRAS|FInstP|MAE}} is the Perren Chair of Astronomy at [[University College London|University College London (UCL)]], 
His research area is Observational Cosmology, in particular probing Dark Matter and Dark Energy. His work involves Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence (AI). 

He was a member of the academi staff at the [[Institute of Astronomy, Cambridge|Institute of Astronomy]] (1990–2003) and a Fellow of [[St Catharine's College, Cambridge]] (1988-2004).
Lahav served as the UCL Head of Astrophysics (2004–2011), 
Vice-Dean (Research) (2011-2015) and Vice-Dean (International) (2020-2026) of the [[UCL Faculty of Mathematical and Physical Sciences|UCL Faculty of Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MAPS)]] and Co-Director of the [[Science and Technology Facilities Council|STFC]] [[Doctoral Training Centre|Centre for Doctoral Training]] in Data Intensive Science.

Lahav was Vice-President of the [[Royal Astronomical Society]] (2010–2012). He is one of the founders of the [[Dark Energy Survey|Dark Energy Survey (DES)]], and he co-chaired the international DES Science Committee from inception until 2016. He chaired both the DES:UK and [[Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument|DESI]]:UK consortia. He previously served as a member of the [[Science and Technology Facilities Council|STFC]] Science Board (2016–2019). From 2012 to 2018, Lahav held a [[European Research Council]] (ERC) Advanced Grant on "Testing the Dark Energy Paradigm".

He is the lead editor of the book ''The Dark Energy Survey: The Story of a Cosmological Experiment'' (World Scientific, 2020).

Hie was a Visiting Fellow at [[All Souls College Oxford]], and he is a Visiting Professor at the [[University of Oxford]] and a Fellow of [[Goodenough College]].

He was awarded the 2026 [[Institute of Physics]] Fred Hoyle Medal and Prize: ''"Ofer Lahav pioneered AI for Astronomy from the early 1990s. His scientific leadership in developing and exploiting the now completed Dark Energy Survey has delivered major advances in precision Cosmology."''

==Education==
Lahav studied physics at [[Tel-Aviv University]] (BSc, 1980), physics at [[Ben-Gurion University of the Negev|Ben-Gurion University]] (MSc, 1985) and earned his PhD (1988) in [[astronomy]]<ref name=ophd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|title=Anisotropies in the local universe|first=Ofer|last=Lahav|date=1988|url=http://ulmss-newton.lib.cam.ac.uk/vwebv/holdingsInfo?bibId=10580|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.279690}}|website=lib.cam.ac.uk|oclc=557212691|archive-date=21 August 2023|access-date=12 December 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230821202219/https://ulmss-newton.lib.cam.ac.uk/vwebv/holdingsInfo?bibId=10580|url-status=dead}}</ref> from the [[University of Cambridge]],

He supervised approximately 30 PhD students and 30 postdoctoral researchers.
